title: RFC 1958 records the principle that end-to-end functions are best realised by end-to-end protocols
summary: RFC 1958 records the principle that end-to-end functions are best realised by end-to-end protocols.
body: RFC 1958, Architectural Principles of the Internet, says it is generally felt that end-to-end functions can best be realised by end-to-end protocols, and it points to the Saltzer, Reed, and Clark argument. The source says: "2.3 It is also generally felt that end-to-end functions can best be realised by end-to-end protocols." The RFC states a design principle used by the Internet's architects. It is not a theorem that no useful function can sit in the network. The Saltzer paper, opened separately, says a low-level version of a function can still be useful as a performance enhancement.

sources.title: RFC 1958: Architectural Principles of the Internet
sources.author: B. Carpenter, editor
